title: SE Rapid Qualify & De-risk Microdeck (wip)
summary: A compact, engineer-focused slide set for SEs to run rapid qualification calls and de-risk early pilots. Prioritizes three minute technical opens, 10 minute SLO/cost tradeoff walkthrough, and an escape-hatch plan for fallbacks and capacity negotiation.
audience: Sales Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Field SEs supporting pilot conversations with engineering/platform teams at mid-market and enterprise accounts.
slides: Title: SE Rapid Qualify & De-risk Microdeck — 6 slides
1) 30s hook: Why inference serving economics changes the pilot (what to say)
2) Quick-qual checklist: three signals we need from the first call (traffic shape, P95 SLO, data residency)
3) Latency-to-value tradeoff visual: sample throughput, batching, and cost knobs (fast/cheap/accurate triangle)
4) Early-fail patterns + escape hatches: fallback routing, degraded model variants, regional fallback
5) Pilot success criteria & minimal telemetry matrix (tokens, KV cache hits, cold-start, error types)
6) Next steps & handoff: engineer playbook, reserved capacity ask template, 2-week proof milestone
speaker_notes: Slide 1 note: Keep the opener pragmatic — say: 'We aim to get you predictable latency under load while keeping cost within your target. We'll show what matters in the first call.'
Slide 2 note: Use this checklist live. If any item is unknown, mark red and promise a follow-up. Ask for sample request sizes and expected concurrency (not just users).
Slide 3 note: Show a simple graph that maps batching, quantization, and prefix caching to dollar/token. Avoid deep model internals unless asked — focus on observable levers the customer can control.

Slide 4 note: Explain a concrete fallback: route to lower-precision variant + regional fallback + rate-limiter-based graceful degradation. Give a one-line code snippet to illustrate toggling a routing policy.
Slide 5 note: Minimal telemetry: per-route p50/p95, token cost, cache hit %, cold-start latency, 500/429 rates. These are the ones we promise to ship to their console within first week of a pilot.
Slide 6 note: Handoff should include a 'reserved-capacity ask' email template the SE can adapt and a 2-week sprint plan with owners (SE, platform engineer, customer eng).
General: Keep language short, action-oriented. Deck is a prompt for conversation, not a spec. Use appendices for deeper model/infra details if the customer asks.
objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: 'We can't share traffic patterns.' -> Rebuttal: Offer a safe sample harness with anonymized request shapes and a small synthetic replay to validate latency assumptions.
Objection: 'We need on-prem / VPC.' -> Rebuttal: Outline private deployment timeline: 4–6 week standard engineering window + guidelines on keys and network prep.
Objection: 'Cost looks high.' -> Rebuttal: Walk through Optimize recommendations — batch profiles and prefix caching can often cut token cost by 30% with minimal latency impact.
Objection: 'What happens on high load spikes?' -> Rebuttal: Describe autoscaling + graceful fallbacks (model variant, regional reroute) and define a runbook for incident initiation.
Objection: 'We need compliance logs.' -> Rebuttal: Point to Private deployment and KMS/HSM integrations; promise audit log retention options and sample schema for logs.
pilot_checklist: Have a small representative payload (5–20k requests) or a replay harness ready
Define two SLOs: user-facing p95 latency and monthly token spend target
Confirm data residency or Private deployment requirement
Identify owner on customer side for quick decisions (network, infra, app lead)
Agree on telemetry shipping (console access + minimum metrics)
negotiation_tips: When asking for reserved capacity, frame it as 'predictable SLA' rather than just price. Offer an introductory month of burst credits to lower initial friction. Have a fallback commercial offer: short-term commit + ramp clause.
usage_instructions: SEs: Use this as a 12-minute live guide. Start with slide 1 hook, run checklist, then dive into tradeoffs. If technical audience asks for deep dive, switch to appendix doc (linked artifact). Update this deck after each pilot with one line: 'what we learned'
next_steps: 1) Run a 30-minute qualification call using this deck; 2) If green, provision a 2-week pilot with telemetry baseline; 3) Capture outcomes and iterate on the deck; assign follow-up in GTM Jira (GTMP-).
risks: Top risk is under-specified traffic leading to wrong capacity sizing. Mitigation: require a synthetic replay and a conservative initial autoscaling policy. Second risk is unclear ownership on customer side—mitigate by getting an owner before pilot kickoff.
